name: B.V.Sc. & A.H. (Bachelor of Veterinary Science and Animal Husbandry)
duration: 5.5 years (4.5 years academic + 1 year compulsory rotating internship)
duration_note: Governed by Veterinary Council of India (VCI) MSVE Regulations. Includes 4.5 professional years of rigorous clinical and livestock coursework followed by a mandatory 12-month paid rotating internship at veterinary hospitals, diagnostic laboratories, and livestock farms.

hero.summary: A 5.5-year clinical and livestock professional degree regulated by the Veterinary Council of India (VCI). Prepares registered veterinary doctors in animal medicine, surgery, reproduction, animal nutrition, pathology, and public health, concluding with a 1-year compulsory internship.

overview.heading: What the B.V.Sc. & A.H. degree covers
paragraphs: Bachelor of Veterinary Science and Animal Husbandry (B.V.Sc. & A.H.) is the statutory professional qualification required to practice veterinary medicine and surgery in India. The programme is strictly governed by the Veterinary Council of India (VCI) under the Minimum Standards of Veterinary Education (MSVE) Regulations.

The degree integrates veterinary medical sciences with animal husbandry and production management. Students undergo intensive training in veterinary anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, pathology, parasitology, microbiology, surgery, radiology, gynecology, obstetrics, and clinical medicine alongside livestock production management, animal genetics, and feeds and nutrition.

Practical clinical training takes place in Veterinary Clinical Complex (VCC) teaching hospitals and Instructional Livestock Farm Complexes (ILFC). In the final year, students complete a compulsory 12-month rotating internship spanning clinical practice, mobile veterinary clinics, slaughterhouse meat inspection, zoo / wildlife exposure, and farm placements.

highlights.label: National entrance
highlights.value: NEET-UG (Mandatory for all admissions in India)

highlights.label: Professional registration
highlights.value: Registration with State Veterinary Council & VCI

who_should_apply: Class 12 biology students passionate about animal health, clinical surgery, companion animal medicine, and wildlife conservation
Candidates qualified in NEET-UG who wish to build a professional medical career treating livestock, pets, poultry, and equine animals
Those keen on public health, zoonotic disease epidemiology, food safety inspection, and vaccine research
Students aiming for gazetted government service as Veterinary Assistant Surgeons or commission in the Indian Army Remount Veterinary Corps (RVC)

curriculum.heading: Professional curriculum framework under VCI MSVE Regulations
curriculum.intro: The B.V.Sc. & A.H. curriculum is structured as a professional year-based system under VCI regulations, combining preclinical, paraclinical, and clinical subjects.

structure.stage: First Professional Year: Pre-Clinical & Husbandry Foundations
structure.focus: Gross and microscopic anatomy, animal physiology, biochemistry, and livestock production systems.
courses: Veterinary Anatomy (osteology, arthrology, myology, neurology, histology)
Veterinary Physiology and Biochemistry
Livestock Production Management (cattle, buffalo, sheep, goat, pig, and horse management)
Instructional livestock farm management practicals

structure.stage: Second Professional Year: Paraclinical Sciences & Breeding
structure.focus: Pathology, microbiology, parasitology, animal genetics, and animal nutrition.
courses: Veterinary Pathology (general, systemic, and avian pathology, necropsy)
Veterinary Microbiology (bacteriology, virology, immunology, mycology)
Veterinary Parasitology (helminthology, entomology, protozoology)
Animal Genetics and Breeding (principles, population genetics, molecular breeding)
Animal Nutrition (ruminant and non-ruminant nutrition, feed technology)

structure.stage: Third Professional Year: Pharmacology & Public Health
structure.focus: Drug actions, clinical pathology, public health, and livestock product technology.
courses: Veterinary Pharmacology and Toxicology (chemotherapy, neuropharmacology)
Veterinary Public Health and Epidemiology (zoonoses, food hygiene)
Veterinary and Animal Husbandry Extension Education
Livestock Products Technology (meat, milk, and wool processing)
Veterinary clinical complex orientation and diagnostic practicals

structure.stage: Fourth Professional Year (1.5 Years): Clinical Disciplines
structure.focus: Comprehensive medicine, anesthesia, surgery, radiology, and animal reproduction.
courses: Veterinary Clinical Medicine (infectious and non-infectious animal diseases)
Veterinary Preventive Medicine and jurisprudence
Veterinary Surgery and Radiology (anesthesia, diagnostic imaging, orthopedic and soft-tissue surgery)
Veterinary Gynaecology and Obstetrics (infertility, artificial insemination, obstetrics)
Veterinary Clinical Complex (VCC) hands-on hospital rotations

structure.stage: Fifth Year: Compulsory Rotating Internship (12 Months)
structure.focus: Full-time practical hospital rotations, field postings, and diagnostic laboratory exposure.
courses: Clinical hospital rotations (medicine, surgery, gynecology)
Ambulatory and emergency veterinary care
Livestock and poultry farm management posting
Meat inspection and slaughterhouse hygiene training
Zoo, wild animal, and equine healthcare exposure

practical_learning.name: Veterinary Clinical Complex (VCC) Postings
practical_learning.description: Daily rotations handling indoor and outdoor animal patients, performing physical examinations, diagnostic ultrasounds, radiography, surgical procedures, and intensive medical care.

practical_learning.name: Instructional Livestock Farm Complex (ILFC)
practical_learning.description: Direct student management of dairy cattle, buffaloes, small ruminants, and poultry farms on university campuses, mastering milking, feed formulation, and artificial insemination.

practical_learning.name: Compulsory Rotating Internship
practical_learning.description: One full calendar year of clinical postings across state veterinary hospitals, disease diagnostic laboratories, dairy processing plants, and zoo reserves.

points: Must have passed the 10+2 qualifying examination with Physics, Chemistry, Biology (or Biotechnology), and English from a recognised education board.
Minimum 50% aggregate marks in Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology, and English (47.5% for SC, ST, and designated reserved categories as per VCI norms).
Candidate must have qualified in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET-UG) of the respective admission year.
Must have attained the minimum age of 17 years on or before 31 December of the year of admission.
Specific physical fitness standards for handling large animals apply.

routes.name: Veterinary Council of India (VCI) 15% All-India Quota
routes.description: Centralized online counselling conducted by VCI based on NEET-UG All-India Ranks for 15% seats across all recognised government veterinary colleges in India.

routes.name: State Veterinary Counselling (85% State Quota)
routes.description: Conducted by respective state veterinary universities or state CET boards based on NEET-UG merit scores for state domicile candidates.

exams.name: NEET-UG
exams.note: Mandatory national entrance exam for 100% of B.V.Sc. & A.H. seats across all veterinary colleges in India.

steps.title: Appear for NEET-UG
steps.text: Register, appear, and qualify in NEET-UG with qualifying percentile.

steps.title: Register for VCI / State Counselling
steps.text: Register for 15% all-India counselling on the official VCI portal and for 85% state quota on your home-state veterinary university portal.

steps.title: Choice Filling & Locking
steps.text: Fill preferences of veterinary colleges based on rank and seat matrix.

steps.title: Physical Reporting & Verification
steps.text: Complete medical fitness examination, document scrutiny, and fee payment at the allotted veterinary college.

documents: Class 10 and 12 marksheet and passing certificates
NEET-UG admit card, rank card, and scorecard
Category and PwBD certificates (if claiming quota)
State domicile certificate for state quota seats
Medical fitness certificate as per VCI format

fees.summary: Tuition fees in government state veterinary universities (such as TANUVAS, GADVASU, LUVAS, MAFSU) are heavily subsidised, generally ranging from ₹20,000 to ₹55,000 per academic year. In private veterinary colleges approved by VCI, annual fees range between ₹3,50,000 to ₹6,50,000 under state quota and higher under management quotas. Interns receive a monthly stipend during their 12-month internship as per university/state norms.

careers.heading: Professional veterinary careers in healthcare, defense, and industry
careers.intro: B.V.Sc. & A.H. graduates become licensed veterinary doctors. The veterinary profession offers diverse opportunities in government animal husbandry departments, the armed forces, companion animal clinics, pharmaceutical research, and commercial dairy and poultry industries.

roles.title: Veterinary Assistant Surgeon (VAS) / Veterinary Officer
roles.description: Class-I / Gazetted medical officer in state animal husbandry departments running veterinary dispensaries and artificial insemination centres.

roles.title: Remount Veterinary Corps (RVC) Officer
roles.description: Commissioned officer (Captain) in the Indian Army responsible for the breeding, healthcare, and training of army horses, mules, and military working dogs.

roles.title: Small Animal / Companion Veterinary Practitioner
roles.description: Independent veterinary clinical practitioner treating domestic pets, performing surgeries, and providing preventative animal healthcare.

roles.title: Dairy & Poultry Technical Consultant
roles.description: Veterinary doctor supervising flock health, bio-security, vaccination, and nutrition in industrial poultry and dairy enterprises.

roles.title: Wildlife & Zoo Veterinarian
roles.description: Specialist providing healthcare, chemical immobilization, disease surveillance, and breeding management for captive and wild animals.

roles.title: Quarantine / Food Safety Inspection Officer
roles.description: Government officer checking livestock imports, animal disease outbreaks, and abattoir meat inspection at ports and borders.

sectors: Commercial Dairy & Poultry Integrators (Amul, Venky's, Suguna)

Indian Army Remount Veterinary Corps (RVC) Direct SSB Commission
Border Security Force (BSF) & ITBP Veterinary Cadre
Central Veterinary Officers (Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying)
Agricultural Scientists Recruitment Board (ASRB - Animal Science disciplines)
higher_study: M.V.Sc. (Master of Veterinary Science) in Surgery, Medicine, Gynaecology, Pathology, etc.
Post-Graduate Diplomas in Small Animal Practice / Wild Animal Health

skills: Veterinary diagnostic clinical examination and case history taking
Soft-tissue and orthopedic veterinary surgery and general anesthesia
Artificial insemination and reproductive ultrasound diagnostics
Livestock herd disease outbreak investigation and biosecurity planning
Necropsy examination and histopathological tissue interpretation
Emergency critical care and fluid therapy in animals

faqs.question: Is NEET-UG compulsory for admission to B.V.Sc. & A.H.?
faqs.answer: Yes. As per the Veterinary Council of India regulations and Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying guidelines, admission to 100% of B.V.Sc. & A.H. seats across all veterinary colleges in India is based strictly on NEET-UG scores.

faqs.question: Can B.V.Sc. & A.H. graduates use the title 'Dr.'?
faqs.answer: Yes. Upon completing B.V.Sc. & A.H. and the compulsory 1-year internship, graduates register with the State Veterinary Council and the Veterinary Council of India, earning the statutory right to practice veterinary medicine and use the title 'Doctor' (Dr.).

faqs.question: Can a veterinary graduate join the Indian Army directly?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Indian Army conducts direct SSB interviews for male and female veterinary graduates to join as commissioned officers with the rank of Captain in the Remount Veterinary Corps (RVC).

faqs.question: What is the duration of B.V.Sc. & A.H. under current regulations?
faqs.answer: Under the VCI MSVE Regulations, the programme spans 5.5 years, comprising 4.5 professional academic years of coursework followed by a compulsory 12-month rotating internship.
